reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) strongly supports boride precipitation and improved grain boundary cohesion in a similar HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy, but it does not provide data on yield strength at high temperature, thermoelastic modulus changes, or the specific NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 system, leaving key premises on mechanical and thermoelastic behavior unsupported.
premises: Boron addition (~0.1 at.%) to a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy induces intergranular precipitation of (Hf, Zr)B2 borides.
These boride precipitates enhance grain boundary cohesion.
Enhanced grain boundary cohesion leads to higher yield strength at high temperatures.
The borides alter dislocation mobility, resulting in a measurable change in thermoelastic modulus.
The effects are expected in the NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy system.
